---
title: "Figure 1.2: LAC: Growth Dispersion"
---

![Python: `python/fig-1-2.py`](../images/python/fig-1-2.png)

Two annual measures of how far growth rates in the region differ, from 2000
to 2025. The first, the average pairwise gap, compares every pair of
countries. The second, the average distance from the median, compares each
country with the middle of the region. Both rise when countries grow at very
different rates, as in crises, and fall when growth is similar across the
region.

**New in this chart:** smoothed lines, with `smooth_line()`.

## The data

Sheet `data`, 26 rows:

| category | Average pairwise gap | Average distance from median |
|---|---|---|
| 2000 | 2.74 | 1.83 |

The years are numbers, so they can be used directly on the x-axis. Each
column is one line, and the column names are the legend labels.

## The script

### Imports and colours

```python
from matplotlib.ticker import MultipleLocator

from chart_style import new_chart, read_chart_data, save_chart, smooth_line
```

Besides the usual helpers, the script imports `smooth_line` from the shared
module and `MultipleLocator` from matplotlib, which is used to set the tick
spacing on both axes.

```python
series_colours = {
    "Average pairwise gap": "#0067A9",
    "Average distance from median": "#00A3AD",
}
```

Blue and teal: two colours of the same family, because the two lines measure
the same thing in two ways.

### The frame

The caption has seven lines and explains both measures. To fit them, the
caption font is reduced to `caption_size=8.2`. `bottom_gap=0.5` leaves
extra room under the plot for the year labels, which are written vertically.

### Smoothed lines

```python
# The Excel chart uses smoothed lines.
for series, colour in series_colours.items():
    ax.plot(*smooth_line(data["category"], data[series]), color=colour,
            linewidth=1.8, solid_capstyle="round", label=series)
```

The Excel chart has the *Smoothed line* option switched on (in *Format Data
Series → Line*). matplotlib has no such option: `ax.plot()` always joins the
points with straight segments. The shared helper `smooth_line(x, y)` fills
the gap. It returns the x and y coordinates of a smooth curve through the 26
points, with 20 points per year. Drawn with straight segments, 500 points
look like a curve.

The `*` in front of `smooth_line(...)` unpacks what the function returns.
`smooth_line()` returns two arrays, x and y, and `*` passes them as the
first two arguments of `ax.plot()`. Without the star you would write:

```python
xs, ys = smooth_line(data["category"], data[series])
ax.plot(xs, ys, color=colour, ...)
```

The curve passes exactly through every data point, so no value is changed:
only the path between points is different. It uses the same method as Excel
(a Catmull-Rom spline), so the two charts match closely. How the curve is
computed is explained in [The shared
layout](../chart-style.qmd#sec-smooth).

Without smoothing, the line would be `ax.plot(data["category"],
data[series], ...)`. Try it to see the difference: with annual data the
straight segments and sharp corners are clearly visible.

### The axes

```python
ax.set_xlim(2000, 2025)
ax.xaxis.set_major_locator(MultipleLocator(5))
ax.tick_params(axis="x", labelrotation=90, direction="in", length=2.3, pad=5)

ax.set_ylim(0, 8)
ax.yaxis.set_major_locator(MultipleLocator(2))
ax.tick_params(axis="y", direction="in", length=2.3, pad=6)
```

- **The x-axis** runs from 2000 to 2025. `MultipleLocator(5)` puts a tick at
  every multiple of 5 within the limits: 2000, 2005, ..., 2025. This is an
  alternative to `ax.set_xticks(range(2000, 2026, 5))`; both give the same
  result here. The labels are written vertically (`labelrotation=90`).
- **No half-step margins.** The lines start and end exactly at the edges of
  the plot, as with Excel's *Axis position: On tick marks* setting. Compare
  [Figure 3.1](fig-3-1.qmd), which leaves half a year at each end.
- **The y-axis** runs from 0 to 8 with a tick every 2.
- **Tick marks point inwards** on both axes (`direction="in"`), as in the
  published chart. See [Tick marks and axis
  lines](../techniques.qmd#sec-ticks).

### The legend

```python
ax.legend(loc="upper left", bbox_to_anchor=(0.05, 0.98),
          handlelength=3.0, labelspacing=0.3)
```

The legend sits in the top left. `labelspacing=0.3` is a little more than
in most charts, because the published chart leaves more space between the
two entries. See [Legends](../techniques.qmd#sec-legends).

## Changing the chart

- **Smoother or rougher curves.** `smooth_line(x, y, points_per_segment=40)`
  uses more points per year. 20 is already more than you can see at this
  size, so this rarely matters.
- **Switching smoothing off.** Replace `*smooth_line(data["category"],
  data[series])` with `data["category"], data[series]`.
- **When not to smooth.** A smoothed curve can overshoot between two points,
  for example below zero next to a sharp fall. For data where that would be
  misleading, use straight lines.

## The complete script

The full `python/fig-1-2.py`, as it runs:

```` {.python filename="python/fig-1-2.py"}
"""Figure 1.2: LAC: Growth Dispersion."""
from matplotlib.ticker import MultipleLocator

from chart_style import new_chart, read_chart_data, save_chart, smooth_line

STEM = "fig-1-2"

data = read_chart_data(STEM)

series_colours = {
    "Average pairwise gap": "#0067A9",
    "Average distance from median": "#00A3AD",
}

fig, ax = new_chart(
    title="LAC: Growth Dispersion",
    subtitle="(Year-over-year percentage change)",
    caption=(
        "Sources: IMF, World Economic Outlook database; and IMF staff\n"
        "calculations.\n"
        "Note: Average pairwise gap is the average absolute difference in growth\n"
        "rates across all country pairs. Average distance from median is the\n"
        "average absolute deviation of each country's growth rate from the regional\n"
        "median. Sample excludes Guyana. LAC = Latin America and the\n"
        "Caribbean."
    ),
    caption_size=8.2,
    left=0.3,
    right=0.2,
    bottom_gap=0.5,
)

# The Excel chart uses smoothed lines.
for series, colour in series_colours.items():
    ax.plot(*smooth_line(data["category"], data[series]), color=colour,
            linewidth=1.8, solid_capstyle="round", label=series)

ax.set_xlim(2000, 2025)
ax.xaxis.set_major_locator(MultipleLocator(5))
ax.tick_params(axis="x", labelrotation=90, direction="in", length=2.3, pad=5)

ax.set_ylim(0, 8)
ax.yaxis.set_major_locator(MultipleLocator(2))
ax.tick_params(axis="y", direction="in", length=2.3, pad=6)

ax.legend(loc="upper left", bbox_to_anchor=(0.05, 0.98),
          handlelength=3.0, labelspacing=0.3)

save_chart(fig, STEM)
````
